# Make Interfaces Feel Better

Curated by Skill Harbor: the small design-engineering details that compound into an interface that feels polished instead of flat, generic, cramped, or unfinished. Salvaged from community practice, it gives concrete, checkable rules rather than vague taste: concentric radius for nested rounded surfaces (outer radius equals inner radius plus padding), optical alignment (geometric centering is not always visual centering, so nudge icon buttons and asymmetric glyphs by eye), borders for separation and focus rings with layered shadows reserved for elevation, and complete interaction states for every control (hover, active, focus, enter, exit, loading, empty). Made for reviewing or improving UI spacing, typography, borders, shadows, motion, hit areas, icons, text wrapping, and interaction states across controls, cards, lists, dashboards, navigation, forms, and toolbars. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; the rules are heuristics for optical coherence, not laws of physics, so apply judgment when a layout fights the formula. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
